newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki again testing records, led by overseas.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki again testing records, led by overseas.

text.p: Imported euphoria swept the bourse back again to new record closing levels on Thursday, with forestries clearly rallying although Nokia lost some momentum after meeting resistance at 500 markka, brokers said.

The FOX portfolio index rose 1.24 percent to 1,257, the HEX all-share index added 1.13 percent to 3,686 -- both just shy of new intrasession bests. Volume was a mighty 917 million markka, but more widely spread than of late with Nokia's share falling.
"People just want to trade, demand is strong," one broker said, as another added that rising knowledge of the Helsinki market overseas was firing interest in a broader range.
Nokia closed up 4.10 markka at 492.00, falling back after running into selling around 497.00.
Some brokers were betting the stock could scale the 500 level in the session -- it only stormed the 400 barrier on July 4. Reaching 500 would bring it up nearly 90 percent on the year.

But UPM played the major role in index gains, making nearly five points of the total 15-point rise as demand for forestries revived after Metsa-Serla beat H1 expectations and sounded upbeat on the year. UPM rose 3.20 markka to 136.60.
Metsa-Serla's gains were more modest after rising sharply ahead of its report: it closed up 0.80 markka at 49.00.
International analysts are taking a selective view on potential gainers in forestry's brightening outlook, and several contacted recently by Reuters said they favoured UPM.

TT Tieto came to life after its H1 came in at the top end of forecasts, closing up 40.00 markka or over eight percent at 520.00 as the flood of liquidity in the current rally washed into a generally less well-known "high tech" play.
But Nokian Renkaat fell 1.50 to 141.50 in unusually heavy volume, about nine percent of the total. Henderson financial management said earlier this week it had lowered its stake.
